name: Acquired Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Acquired Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of polyuria (>3 L/day) and polydipsia
Demonstrated low or absent plasma arginine vasopressin levels despite hyperosmolarity
Failure to concentrate urine during water deprivation test with improvement after desmopressin administration
MRI evidence of hypothalamic or pituitary stalk abnormalities
Exclusion of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and primary polydipsia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of polyuria and polydipsia with low plasma vasopressin levels and positive response to desmopressin during water deprivation test
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of polyuria and polydipsia.

imaging: MRI showing absence or reduced pituitary bright spot
other: Positive response to desmopressin administration confirming central origin

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated plasma vasopressin levels
Often associated with renal tubular dysfunction
Low serum sodium due to water overload
Urine osmolality normalizes with water deprivation

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe polyuria and hypernatremia
Neurological symptoms such as seizures or coma
Failure to respond to fluid replacement without desmopressin
references: Orphanet: Acquired Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency - ORPHA:95626
NICE Clinical Guidelines on Diabetes Insipidus
